$comment: p15-oracle-072: the browser, browserProfile and devtools action families (every non-excluded id of plans/cmux-next/action-surfaces.json whose family is browser, browserProfile or devtools: 123 today, the design's 113 plus ids added since). gen_actions.py (p15-oracle-071) reads this file the way gen_daemon_ops.py reads daemon-ops/<family>/_tuning.json (oracle.py skips _ files) and writes one case per action and engine into the flat actions suite. Each entry was reviewed against its handler; `engines.webkit` overrides keys for a WebKit page (test phase: green twice on both engines). Keys: context (a contexts entry the case sets up before the action, or none; a context's fixture is merged into the case's fixture and its depends_on names the WORK.tsv tasks its setup needs), entrypoint (key | action | cli, with `cli` the argv of the action's own CLI verb; absent: the generator's choice, the single-stroke shortcut when there is one; an error expectation runs through action.run, whose refusal carries the typed details: driver_app.py compares errorDetails with the reply's error.data; a cli, key or mcp reply carries none), params (action.run arguments), before and after (steps around the action: {id, action, params?, target?, focus?} runs action.run on the current target (focus: true is action.run's focus: the run may change focus and selection as a person's would, ControlActionRequest.focus), {id, keys, waitFor?} sends keystrokes, {id, cli} runs the bundle's cmux with that argv, {id, waitFor} settles), expect (case-v1 expect: the ActionEffect kind as receipt, or the typed error and the details it must carry; an action.run refusal is control.unavailable, a disabled action control.disabled, both with data.action), waitFor (case-v1 waitFor after the action; a pointer that starts with $page is relative to the context's page pointer), invariants (case-specific statements for the reviewer; I1-I18 run anyway), untested, note, chromium (the Chromium file the behavior copies), divergence (keys of divergences, each a finding against Chrome's design or the budget contract, filed here for routing; the case is still green because the oracle is differential), gap (the whole action is blocked; it names the WORK.tsv task that closes it) and gap_success (the case runs the refusal or no-op the app gives in the fixture; the success path waits for the named WORK.tsv task, whose spec makes that fixture). An engine override with a null value removes the key for that engine. Legacy bind/run handlers report action.done (Action.run); browser.link.openInSplit is the family's one bindEffect handler (waiting, daemonEcho).

page.note: the fixture page in the focused pane: p15-oracle-222's loopback load.html (openBrowser and cmux browser navigate refuse data: URLs, BrowserURLResolver searches them), opened with focus so the socket caller's tab is selected and focused (without it TabLifecycle.newBrowser opens it unselected behind the focused tab), then navigated to #b by the bundle's CLI (a same-document navigation), so it has two history entries. The tabs facet lists a pane's browser and page tabs only (OracleTabsFacet), so on a fresh launch per case (--batch-limit 1) the fixture is the one tab of pane 0's list: page-only checks that before any case reads $page

case-schema-digit-ids.what: schemas/oracle/case-v1.schema.json $defs/argsActionRun/properties/action has the pattern ^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\.[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)*$, which refuses a segment that starts with a digit; the catalog has four such ids (browser.keepNeighborTabsAwake.0-3), the only ones in action-surfaces.json. A pattern of ^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\.[A-Za-z0-9]+)*$ would let gen_actions.py write an action.run step for every catalog id.
case-schema-digit-ids.chromium: chrome/app/chrome_command_ids.h (every command has an id the test harness can name)
case-schema-digit-ids.case: the four cases run the action's own CLI verb (an entrypoint it offers) until the pattern changes

hard-reload-chromium.what: Hard Reload refuses on a Chromium page (MiscHandlerStrings.hardReloadEngine): only WebKitTab reloads from origin. Chrome's Shift-Cmd-R reloads bypassing the cache on every page.
hard-reload-chromium.case: expects the refusal on chromium, so the case is green and a fix shows as a base/head divergence

devtools-untracked-work.what: DevToolsHandlers.runChromium sends its protocol calls (and evaluate its page scripts) in an unstructured Task with try?: the registry never tracks the work, action.run answers before it applies, and a failure is dropped. The budget contract wants the handler to return the work as an ActionEffect (applied with a rollback, or waiting) so the registry sends, tracks and reports it.
devtools-untracked-work.chromium: content/browser/devtools/protocol/ (each command answers its own result; DevTools front end front_end/core/sdk shows a failed command)
devtools-untracked-work.case: the settled checkpoint can come before the protocol call applies; no facet reads that state yet, so the case stays green, and a facet of the page's emulation would make it flaky until fixed

PageInfoController.unavailableReason only covers reenableCertificateWarnings.

page-info-silent-no-origin.case: aboutThisPage expects ok with no change on the loopback page, which is what the app does today; the other three run their success path on the loopback origin, so their silent return was found by reading the handler

settings-untracked-write.what: The handler applies the value at once, then writes cmux-next.json in an unstructured Task whose failure is only logged: the registry does not track the write, so action.run can answer before the settings facet shows it.
settings-untracked-write.chromium: components/prefs/pref_service.cc SetValue (the pref store commits on the UI thread's own call; the write to disk is ImportantFileWriter's, never the caller's)
settings-untracked-write.case: the cases wait for the settings facet (waitFor), so they stay deterministic

profile-untracked-create.what: The handler starts createWorkspace in an unstructured Task with try?: a failure is dropped and the registry does not track the window or workspace it makes.
